get.summary: List the calling key's user's API keys.
get.description: Lists the active keys belonging to the calling key's user, oldest first, with the total. Returns each key's ID, prefix, scopes, creation time, and whether it is the bootstrap key, never the key itself. session=true lists only session keys and session=false only long-lived keys; total counts only the keys listed. Requires the `api-keys:read` scope.

parameters.description: true lists only session keys, false only long-lived keys; left out, both. total counts only the keys listed.
parameters.name: session

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold api-keys:read.

post.summary: Create an API key for the calling key's user.
post.description: Mints a key for the calling key's user, so a key can be rotated without an administrator. The scopes must be a subset of those the calling key holds. The key is returned once: only its hash is stored. Recorded as an api_key_created audit event naming the calling user and API key. Requires the `api-keys:write` scope.

201.description: The key was created. The value is returned here and nowhere else.

400.description: No scopes were given, or one of them is not a scope.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold api-keys:write, is a session key, or a requested scope is not held by the calling key.

delete.summary: Sign out: revoke the calling session key.
delete.description: Revokes the session key making the request, so a person can sign out without an administrator. Any key may call it, whatever its scopes, because it can only end the caller's own access. A long-lived key cannot revoke itself; revoke it with another key. Recorded as an api_key_deleted audit event with the reason signed out.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

409.description: The calling key is a long-lived key, not a session key.

get.description: Returns every scope an API key can carry, with what it allows, in the order Philter declares them, so a client offering scopes to choose from need not hard-code them. Any key may call it, whatever its scopes, since it describes the API rather than any account.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

delete.description: Revokes a key: it stops authenticating at once and cannot be restored. The key making the request cannot revoke itself; revoke it with another key. The calling key cannot revoke a key holding a scope it does not hold. A caller can revoke its own user's keys; an administrator can revoke any user's. Recorded as an api_key_deleted audit event naming the calling user and API key. Requires the `api-keys:write` scope.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold api-keys:write, or the key being revoked holds a scope the calling key does not.

404.description: There is no active key with that ID that the caller may manage.

409.description: The key is the one making the request.

put.description: Replaces the scopes on a key. The key value does not change. The new scopes must be a subset of those the calling key holds, and the calling key cannot change a key holding a scope it does not hold. The key making the request cannot change its own scopes. A caller can change its own user's keys; an administrator can change any user's. Recorded as an api_key_scopes_changed audit event with the scopes before and after and the calling user and API key. Requires the `api-keys:write` scope.

400.description: No scopes were given, or one of them is not a scope.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold api-keys:write, a requested scope is not held by the calling key, the key being changed holds a scope the calling key does not, or the calling key is a session key and the change adds a scope.

404.description: There is no active key with that ID that the caller may manage.

409.description: The key is the one making the request.

get.description: Returns audit events, most recent first, paginated. Filter by event type with event, by time with from and to (ISO-8601 instants; from is inclusive, to is exclusive), and by acting principal with owner. Reading the audit log is itself audited. The log covers the whole deployment, so this requires an administrator as well as the audit:read scope. Requires the `audit:read` scope.

400.description: A timestamp could not be parsed, the range is reversed, or the event type is not one Philter emits.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold audit:read, or the caller is not an administrator.

404.description: The owner does not exist, or the caller may not reach it. The API does not distinguish the two, so an owner value cannot be used to discover accounts.

get.summary: Export the audit log as CSV.
get.description: Returns the audit log for a range of whole days as CSV, most recent first. from and to are dates (YYYY-MM-DD), both inclusive, read in zone (an IANA time zone such as UTC or America/New_York), or in the server's time zone when zone is omitted. to may be at most 30 days after from. Returns up to limit events (default 100, at most 1000; a larger value is treated as the maximum, and zero or less as the default), starting offset events into the range; the X-Philter-Export-Truncated header is true when more remain, and X-Philter-Export-Next-Offset gives the offset to request next. Events are ordered by timestamp and then id, so paging a range that is no longer receiving events returns each exactly once; a range that includes the current day can repeat events across pages. Timestamps in the CSV are UTC. The export is itself audited. Requires an administrator as well as the audit:read scope. Requires the `audit:read` scope.

200.description: The CSV. Headers give the row count, whether it was truncated, and the time zone used.

400.description: A date is missing or not YYYY-MM-DD, the range is reversed or longer than the maximum, the zone is not a time zone, offset is negative or not a number, or limit is not a number. The body says which.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

post.summary: Redact text and explain the redactions.
post.description: Redacts the plain-text request body using the given policy and context, returning the filtered text together with an explanation of every span that was redacted (type, position, and applied filter). Use the c query parameter to select a context and p to select a policy. When output signing is enabled in Admin Settings, the response includes an `X-Philter-Signature` header containing an ES256 JWT that binds the SHA-256 hash of the response body, the applied policy name and version, a per-response UUID, and an issue timestamp. Verify the signature using the public key from `GET /api/signing-key`. Pass sign=true to request a signature when the deployment has not enabled signing. The admin setting is a floor: with it on every response is signed and sign=false does not change that. Requires the `redact` scope.

200.description: Full text filter result with governing policy metadata.

401.description: Unauthorized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: Not Found

500.description: Signing is enabled but the signing operation failed.

post.description: Requires the `redact` scope. Text is synchronous and returns text/plain. For PDFs select application/pdf or application/zip with Accept. PDFs default to async=true, returning application/json with documentId regardless of the selected download format. Set async=false for inline binary output. Async submission captures resolved configuration. Pass sign=true to request a signature when the deployment has not enabled signing. The admin setting is a floor: with it on every response is signed and sign=false does not change that. It applies to the text path, which is the one that is signed; sign=true on a PDF request is refused with 400 rather than answered unsigned.

post.description: Creates a named hold that blocks deletion and purge of the specified evidence until the hold is released. The reference must be unique for the calling user. Two scope types are supported: 'document_chain' protects a specific document's ledger chain; 'user' protects all governance evidence owned by the hold's owner, which is the caller or the user named by owner. For a user hold, scopeValue is optional; if given it must be the owner's username, and the owner's username is stored either way. Admins may place a hold on another user's evidence via the owner parameter. Requires the `holds:write` scope.

Releasing a hold is audited. Admins may release another user's hold via the owner parameter. Requires the `holds:write` scope.

Admins may purge another user's entries by passing that user's username as owner, which additionally requires ADMIN_CROSS_USER_ACCESS_ENABLED=true. Requires the `ledger:delete` scope.

get.summary: Get Philter's limits and the caller's capabilities.
get.description: Returns the sizes, lengths, and name rules Philter enforces, the session key timeouts, and what the caller may do: their role, how many contexts they have, and whether they may reach other users' resources or delete ledger chains. Each value is the one Philter enforces, including any set through its environment variable. Any key may call it, whatever its scopes, including a session key that must first change its password or enroll in MFA, since it describes the API and the caller's own access. For an administrator, crossUserAccess and ledgerDeletion reflect ADMIN_CROSS_USER_ACCESS_ENABLED and LEDGER_DELETION_ENABLED; for anyone else they are false, so the response does not reveal those settings.

409.description: The policy was not replaced, and reason says why: policy_managed (a managed policy, which cannot be replaced) or policy_changed (it changed concurrently; reload it and retry).

post.description: Creates a new policy named by name from one of the caller's policies or, for a name starting with managed_, from a built-in managed policy. The copy has the source's policy and description; a copy of a managed policy notes which one it came from, and a copy of the caller's own policy keeps its notes. The copy starts its own version history and is active at once. Admins may copy within another user's account by passing that user's username as owner. Requires the `policies:write` scope.

400.description: The new name is missing or invalid.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: There is no such policy to copy, or the owner does not exist or the caller may not reach it.

409.description: A policy with the new name already exists; reason is policy_exists.

get.description: Returns a policy's name, description, notes, current revision, whether it is a built-in managed policy, and when it was created and last updated: everything except the policy itself. A name starting with managed_ returns that managed policy's details. Admins may read another user's by passing that user's username as owner. Requires the `policies:read` scope.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: There is no such policy, or the owner does not exist or the caller may not reach it.

put.summary: Set a policy's description and notes.
put.description: Sets the description (up to 200 characters) and notes (up to 1000). A field left out is left as it is; an empty value clears it. They are not part of the policy, so this does not create a new version. Managed policies cannot be changed. Admins may change another user's by passing that user's username as owner. Requires the `policies:write` scope.

200.description: The policy's details after the change.

400.description: The description or notes are too long.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: There is no such policy, or the owner does not exist or the caller may not reach it.

409.description: The policy is a managed policy; reason is policy_managed.

get.summary: Diff two revisions of a policy.
get.description: Returns an RFC 6902 JSON Patch array describing what changed between the 'from' revision and the 'to' revision. If from and to are omitted, the two most recent retained revisions are compared. Object-level changes (adds, removes, replaces) are reported per field path; array values that differ are reported as a single replace at the array path. Each replace and remove also carries oldValue, the value before the change, so a client can show both sides; RFC 6902 has a client applying the patch ignore it. Admins may diff another user's policy via owner. Requires the `policies:read` scope.

200.description: Revision diff; value is omitted for removals.

400.description: The policy name is missing, fewer than two retained revisions exist for a default diff, or only one of from/to was supplied.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: The policy or a requested revision does not exist.

post.summary: Roll back a policy to a prior revision.
post.description: Restores the content of the specified revision as a new head revision, preserving the full history. The live policy is updated with the prior content and its revision counter is incremented. The rollback is audited. Admins may roll back another user's policy via the owner parameter. Requires the `policies:write` scope.

201.description: Rollback succeeded. Body contains the new revision number.

400.description: The policy name or target revision is missing.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: The policy or the target revision does not exist; the message says which. No body when the owner does not exist or the caller may not reach it.

409.description: The policy was not rolled back, and reason says why: policy_managed (managed policies cannot be rolled back) or policy_changed (the policy changed concurrently; reload it and retry).

get.summary: List retained versions of a policy.
get.description: Returns a summary of each retained snapshot for the named policy, ordered by revision descending (most recent first). Each entry carries the revision number, the timestamp the snapshot was captured, its content hash, and the username of the user whose change produced it. The history of a deleted policy is kept and listed the same way; GET /api/policies?deleted=true lists deleted policies. Admins may browse another user's history via the owner parameter. Requires the `policies:read` scope.

200.description: A page of version summaries, most recent first by default, and the total.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: The named policy does not exist, or a non-admin caller named another user as owner.

get.summary: Fetch a specific revision of a policy.
get.description: Returns the full policy JSON as it existed at the given revision. The response shape is identical to GET /api/policies/{policyName}. Admins may fetch another user's revision via the owner parameter. Requires the `policies:read` scope.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: The policy or the requested revision does not exist.

get.summary: Get the always-redact and never-redact lists.
get.description: Returns the account's always-redact and never-redact lists, and each list's revision for If-Match on PUT /api/redact-lists/{list}. Both lists are always present; an account with no saved terms returns empty arrays. Admins may read another user's lists by passing that user's username as owner. Requires the `lists:read` scope.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: The owner does not exist, or the caller may not reach it. The API does not distinguish the two, so an owner value cannot be used to discover accounts.

post.summary: Replace the always-redact and never-redact lists.
post.description: Replaces both lists in full with the supplied contents - this is not a merge. Each field is the complete desired contents of that list; a list that is omitted or sent as an empty array is cleared. Terms are trimmed and blank entries are dropped. Each list may contain up to 1000 terms, and each term may be up to 100 characters. Both lists move to their next revision. Takes no If-Match; to replace one list on the condition that it has not changed, use PUT /api/redact-lists/{list}. Admins may replace another user's lists by passing that user's username as owner. Requires the `lists:write` scope.

400.description: The request body is malformed, a list has too many terms, or a term is too long.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: The owner does not exist, or the caller may not reach it. The API does not distinguish the two, so an owner value cannot be used to discover accounts.

put.summary: Append to the always-redact and never-redact lists.
put.description: Appends the supplied terms to the existing lists rather than replacing them - use POST to replace. Each field's terms are added to the current contents of that list; a list that is omitted or sent as an empty array is left unchanged. Terms are trimmed, blank entries are dropped, and terms already present are not added again. The resulting list may contain up to 1000 terms, and each term may be up to 100 characters; an append that would exceed the limit is rejected. Each list appended to moves to its next revision. Admins may append to another user's lists by passing that user's username as owner. Requires the `lists:write` scope.

400.description: The request body is malformed, the resulting list has too many terms, or a term is too long.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: The owner does not exist, or the caller may not reach it. The API does not distinguish the two, so an owner value cannot be used to discover accounts.

get.description: Returns one list, always or never, and its revision. The ETag header carries the revision too, quoted. Send it back in If-Match when replacing the list with PUT /api/redact-lists/{list}. A list never written is empty, at revision 0. Admins may read another user's list by passing that user's username as owner. Requires the `lists:read` scope.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: The list is not always or never, or the owner does not exist or the caller may not reach it. The API does not distinguish the two, so an owner value cannot be used to discover accounts.

put.description: Replaces one list, always or never, in full with the terms in the body, leaving the other list as it is, and moves it to its next revision. Send the revision you read in If-Match, quoted as the ETag gives it, so the write is refused with 409 and reason redact_list_changed if someone changed the list since; without If-Match the list is replaced whatever its revision. Terms are trimmed and blank entries are dropped. The list may contain up to 1000 terms, and each term may be up to 100 characters. Admins may replace another user's list by passing that user's username as owner. Requires the `lists:write` scope.

200.description: The list was replaced. The body and the ETag header give its new revision.

400.description: The request body is malformed, the list has too many terms, a term is too long, or If-Match is not a revision.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: The list is not always or never, or the owner does not exist or the caller may not reach it. The API does not distinguish the two, so an owner value cannot be used to discover accounts.

409.description: The list is no longer at the revision given in If-Match. Nothing was written. Read the list again and retry.

post.description: Reverses one or more values that were redacted via the CRYPTO_REPLACE or FPE_ENCRYPT_REPLACE strategy. The caller must supply a stated reason, which is recorded in the audit log alongside the actor, timestamp, and count of reversals. A user may re-identify their own values; an admin may re-identify any user's values by supplying that user's username via the owner parameter. CRYPTO_REPLACE requires policyName so the key can be resolved from the stored policy. FPE_ENCRYPT_REPLACE uses the user's per-account FPE key; if the policy specified a custom FPE configuration, also pass policyName so its key and tweak are used instead. Requires the `reidentify` scope.

401.description: Missing or invalid API key.

403.description: Insufficient scope, disabled API, or access denied.

404.description: Named policy not found, or owner not found.

get.description: Returns the deployment's admin settings. The Phield API key is never returned, only whether one is set. Also returns, read-only, whether cross-user access and ledger deletion are enabled and whether the signing key is externally managed, which are set by environment variables. Requires an administrator as well as the scope. Requires the `settings:read` scope.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold settings:read, or the caller is not an administrator.

patch.description: Changes the settings given in the body and leaves the rest as they are. An empty phieldApiKey removes the key. phieldUrl must be an absolute http or https URL, and is required while Phield is enabled; both are checked when a request changes Phield. Each webhookAllowlist entry must be a hostname, an IP address, or a CIDR range. Nothing is changed if any value is invalid. Returns the settings as saved, with warnings, such as a Phield API key that will be sent over http. Recorded as a settings_updated audit event naming the settings that changed and the calling API key, not their values. The read-only crossUserAccessEnabled, ledgerDeletionEnabled, and signingKeyExternallyManaged are ignored. Requires an administrator as well as the scope. Requires the `settings:write` scope.

400.description: A value is invalid. The body says which, and nothing was changed.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold settings:write, or the caller is not an administrator.

get.description: Tells a sign-in page, before anyone has signed in, that password sign-in is enabled, and gives the rules a password must meet, for a page where a person sets one. Requires no API key. Returns 404 unless PASSWORD_SIGN_IN_ENABLED is true, as the other sign-in endpoints do, so a 404 means password sign-in is not available.

401.description: Unauthorized

404.description: Password sign-in is not enabled.

post.description: Takes a username and password. For a user enrolled in MFA, returns a single-use challenge that expires in five minutes; send it with a code to POST /api/sign-in/mfa to get the key. Otherwise returns a session key for the user, which expires after SESSION_KEY_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MINUTES without a request or SESSION_KEY_MAX_LIFETIME_MINUTES after issue. The key holds every scope, with the user's role still deciding administrator access, but cannot create API keys. A user who must change their password, or must enroll in MFA, gets a key that can only do that and sign out. A wrong password, an unknown user, a user without a password, and a deactivated user all get the same 401. Requires no API key. Returns 404 unless PASSWORD_SIGN_IN_ENABLED is true. Recorded as sign_in_succeeded or sign_in_failed with the username and client IP address, never the password.

200.description: Signed in, or, for a user enrolled in MFA, a challenge. A session key is returned here and nowhere else.

401.description: The username or password is not valid.

403.description: The password is right, but the user's MFA is locked after repeated bad codes. An administrator must unlock it.

404.description: Password sign-in is not enabled.

429.description: The username is locked after repeated failures (POST /api/sign-in only), or the client address is over SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE. Retry-After gives the seconds to wait, and reason says which: locked or rate_limited.

post.summary: Complete sign-in with an MFA code.
post.description: Takes the challenge POST /api/sign-in returned and a code from the user's authenticator app, and returns the session key. The challenge is used up by any attempt, right or wrong, so a wrong code means signing in again. Each code is accepted once. The fifth consecutive bad code locks the user until an administrator unlocks them. Requires no API key. Returns 404 unless PASSWORD_SIGN_IN_ENABLED is true. Recorded as sign_in_succeeded or sign_in_failed.

200.description: Signed in. The session key is returned here and nowhere else.

401.description: The challenge is unknown, used, or expired, or the code is not valid.

403.description: The user's MFA is locked after repeated bad codes.

404.description: Password sign-in is not enabled.

429.description: The username is locked after repeated failures (POST /api/sign-in only), or the client address is over SIGN_IN_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE. Retry-After gives the seconds to wait, and reason says which: locked or rate_limited.

get.description: Returns the operator's ES256 (ECDSA P-256) public signing key in PEM, JWK, and fingerprint form. Use the public key to verify the `X-Philter-Signature` JWT header returned on successful `POST /api/filter` and `POST /api/explain` responses when output signing is enabled. This endpoint does not require authentication.

401.description: Unauthorized

post.description: Generates a new ES256 keypair and makes it the active signing key. The superseded key is retained and stays retrievable through GET /api/signing-key/{keyId}, so signatures and ledger entries made with it remain verifiable; consumers should resolve each signature's key id rather than caching one key. Rotation is the response to a suspected key compromise, so it requires an administrator as well as the signing:write scope, and is recorded as a signing_key_regenerated audit event. Requires the `signing:write` scope.

200.description: The key that is now active.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold signing:write, or the caller is not an administrator.

409.description: The signing key is managed by PHILTER_SIGNING_KEY_PATH and cannot be rotated through the API.

get.summary: Get a specific public signing key.
get.description: Returns a retained public signing key by its id, in PEM form. A key that has been superseded by a regeneration is kept, because redaction-ledger entries signed with it must remain verifiable. Ledger entries and exports name the key that signed them in their signingKeyId field. This endpoint does not require authentication.

401.description: Unauthorized

404.description: No key with that id is retained.

get.description: Lists users sorted by username, including deactivated users, with the total count. Requires an administrator as well as the scope. Requires the `users:read` scope.

post.description: Creates a user with a default policy and context. The role is user unless admin is given. A password is optional; without one the user can only use API keys, created with POST /api/users/{username}/api-keys. A user created with a password must change it at next sign-in, and setting it is audited as user_password_set. Requires an administrator as well as the scope. Recorded as a user_created audit event naming the calling administrator as the principal and the calling API key in the details. Requires the `users:write` scope.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold users:write, or the caller is not an administrator.

409.description: A user with that username already exists, active or deactivated.

Enrollment takes effect only once POST /api/users/me/mfa/confirm sees a valid code; starting again replaces an unconfirmed secret. Requires the mfaAvailable setting, and the scope but not an administrator. Requires the `users:write` scope.

Revokes the user's session keys, so the person signs in again with MFA. Requires the scope but not an administrator. Recorded as a user_mfa_enrolled audit event. Requires the `users:write` scope.

Recorded as a user_password_changed audit event, without either password. Requires the `users:write` scope.

get.description: Lists the user's webhook deliveries, newest first, with each one's status, attempts, last error, and when it was queued, last changed, is next due, and was delivered, so a failing webhook can be diagnosed. The secret and the event body are not included. A delivery that ended, delivered or failed, is kept for WEBHOOK_DELIVERIES_TTL_SECONDS (30 days by default). Paged with offset and limit (25 by default, at most 100). Admins may list another user's deliveries via the owner parameter. Requires the `webhooks:read` scope.

200.description: A page of deliveries and the total.

401.description: The Authorization header is absent or the API key is not recognized.

403.description: The key does not hold webhooks:read.

404.description: The owner does not exist, or the caller may not reach it.

post.summary: Send a test event to the webhook.
post.description: Sends one signed WEBHOOK_TEST event to the webhook now, signed and checked against the destination allowlist as a real delivery is, and returns what happened: whether the receiver answered 2xx, its status code, and any error. The event is not queued or retried and does not appear in GET /api/webhook/deliveries. Its body has "test": true so a receiver can ignore it. Waits for the receiver up to WEBHOOK_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and WEBHOOK_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. Admins may test another user's webhook via the owner parameter. Recorded as a webhook_tested audit event with the outcome; the URL and secret are not recorded. Requires the `webhooks:write` scope.
